key_insight: Introduce Reflective Test-Time Planning, enabling embodied LLM agents to turn repeated trials into accumulated experience by combining immediate candidate scoring with post-trial reflection to avoid repeating mistakes.
problem_solved: Embodied agents often repeat the same failures at deployment because they treat each attempt independently; this work enables agents to diagnose, learn from, and adapt after mistakes without full offline retraining.
method: Reflection-in-action: at test time, scale internal generation to propose multiple candidate actions and score/rank them with an internal critic before execution.

Reflection-on-action: after attempts, run a post-hoc analysis of failures to extract corrective insights (e.g., failure causes, better examples or prompts) and update planning heuristics or few-shot context for subsequent trials.
impact: Makes embodied LLMs more robust and sample-efficient in real-world deployments by converting errors into adaptive knowledge, reducing repeated failures and improving task success over repeated trials.
visual_elements: Loop diagram: trial → execute candidate actions → reflect (in-action) → execute chosen action → reflect (on-action) → update planner
Before/after bar chart showing reduced failure repetition and improved success rate across trials
Timeline/accumulation graphic showing knowledge or prompt/context updates across successive trials
Icons: robot arm, LLM/brain, checklist/critic scorecard to represent generation, scoring, and reflection
paper_title: Learning from Trials and Errors: Reflective Test-Time Planning for Embodied LLMs
paper_authors: Yining Hong, Huang Huang, Manling Li, Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu
